consequence-01.why: par conséquent links two independent sentences and introduces a result. parce que introduces a cause, reversing cause and effect; grâce à needs a noun.

consequence-02.why: Before an adjective (fatigué), si or tellement + que expresses a result. tant is for verbs; tant de is for nouns.

consequence-03.why: Before a noun (monde) you need tellement de / tant de. si is only for adjectives and adverbs; tellement is missing de.

consequence-04.why: To modify a verb, use tellement or tant (between the auxiliary and the past participle). si can’t modify a verb; tellement de needs a noun.

consequence-05.why: si bien que + indicative introduces a result (having to move house). parce que and puisque introduce causes, reversing cause and effect.

consequence-06.why: de sorte que + indicative expresses a result that actually happened (ont télétravaillé). afin que and pour que express purpose and take the subjunctive.

consequence-07.why: Only a noun phrase follows (notre retard), so d’où + noun. donc and si bien que need a full sentence.

consequence-08.why: c’est pourquoi + full sentence introduces a result. d’où only takes a noun; faute de expresses a cause (lack) and takes a noun.

consequence-09.why: Before an adverb (vite) use si or tellement. tant modifies verbs; tant de modifies nouns.

consequence-10.why: The intensity structure before a noun: tant de + noun + que. si de doesn’t exist; trop de… que can’t form a result structure (trop goes with pour).

consequence-11.why: To modify a verb (pleuvait), use tellement or tant after the verb. si only modifies adjectives/adverbs; tellement de needs a noun.

consequence-12.why: The fixed structure au point que + indicative (to the point that). à point and du point can’t form this expression of result.

consequence-13.why: An infinitive follows (se blesser) and the subject is the same, so au point de + infinitive. au point que and si bien que need a clause.

consequence-14.why: In writing, ainsi (or aussi) at the start of a sentence can trigger subject–verb inversion: ainsi l’entreprise a-t-elle… alors and donc don’t trigger inversion at the start of a sentence, so the inverted structure doesn’t fit them.

consequence-15.why: Before the adjective nombreux use si (or tellement). tant modifies verbs; tant de modifies nouns.

consequence-16.why: c’est pour cela que + full sentence introduces a result. d’où takes a noun; grâce à quoi signals a positive result, contradicting “unable to call for help”.

consequence-17.why: The second half (not having revised enough) is the cause, so car. d’où only takes a noun, not a clause; au point que introduces a result (to the point that), reversing cause and effect.

consequence-18.why: The second half (failing the exam) is the result, so si bien que + indicative. car introduces a cause, reversing cause and effect; d’où only takes a noun (d’où son échec), not a clause.

consequence-19.why: A noun phrase follows (la nécessité de…) with no conjugated verb, so only d’où works. de sorte que and c’est pourquoi need a full sentence.

consequence-20.why: Before the noun succès use tant de (or tellement de). tant alone modifies verbs; si modifies adjectives/adverbs.

consequence-21.why: Before the adjective émue use tellement (or si). In modern French tant doesn’t modify adjectives; tant de modifies nouns.

consequence-22.why: si bien que expresses an actual result and takes the indicative: il est arrivé. soit arrivé is subjunctive; arriver is the infinitive and can’t be the verb of a clause.

consequence-23.why: Here de sorte que expresses a result that has happened, so the indicative: les prix ont diminué. aient is subjunctive (used only when de sorte que expresses purpose); avoir is the infinitive.

consequence-24.why: par conséquent stands alone, followed by a comma and a full sentence. en conséquence de must be followed by a noun; à la suite is missing de + noun.

consequence-25.why: si… que expresses a result and takes the indicative: ont fermé. aient fermé is subjunctive; fermer is the infinitive.

consequence-26.why: tant de… que is a correlative structure; the second part is just que. si bien and de sorte lack que and can’t pair with tant de.

consequence-27.why: si + adjective + que expresses a result. trop goes with pour (que) (trop bruyant pour que…); tant doesn’t modify adjectives.

consequence-28.why: In speech, alors introduces a result (so). car and puisque introduce causes, reversing cause and effect.

consequence-29.why: donc can go between the auxiliary and the past participle: nous sommes donc allés. d’où takes a noun; si bien lacks que and can’t go in this position.

consequence-30.why: en conséquence on its own means “consequently” (formal). en conséquence de needs a noun; par conséquence is a common error for par conséquent.
